android.notes:
A guide, in the app. First launch now walks seven cards — what each screen is, with a picture of it — and there is a Guide tab beside the gesture list you can go back to any time, from the home screen or the + button. Every button it names is drawn rather than spelled out.

Send your marks as marks. Sharing can now send an InForm file instead of burning the drawings in: the person you send it to opens it and the arrows and angles are still arrows and angles, movable, answerable, and sendable back. Burning them in is still the default, because that plays anywhere.

A real share screen. Save and Share now ask the same first question — a screenshot of this frame, the loop region, or the whole video — and answer it from where your cues are. Your written notes ride along as the message text, voice notes attach as files, and the phone's own apps are IN the screen: tap one and it has gone.

Timecodes in a note. The clock button writes the moment you are on into the note wherever the cursor is, without raising the keyboard, so you can mark several things while the clip runs. Tap any time you have written and the video jumps there.

Land a loop cue on the exact frame. Tap a loop handle to arm it — the handle and the step arrows both turn amber — and each press of an arrow walks that cue one frame, with the video following. It is the only way to place a cue on a frame your fingertip is covering.

The visibility band now lines up with the scrub bar above it, so a drawing's window reads against the same track everywhere.
